Spontaneous Communications: The public is encouraged to address the Parks & Recreation Commission on any matter listed on the
agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments on items listed
on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments
on matters not listed on the agenda during the Spontaneous Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The Parks & Recreation Commission may request from staff to investigate and/or
schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Commission or City Council meeting.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a Commission meeting
or other services offered by this City, please contact City Hall at (626) 430-2200. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Chief Deputy City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda
packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with disabilities. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to
the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to
provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Staff reports are available for inspection at the office of the Chief Deputy City Clerk, City Hall, 5050 N. Irwindale Avenue,
during regular business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday).

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commission

member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to three minutes unless
such time limits are extended.

The Irwindale PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION met in regular session at the above time
and place.

ROLL CALL:  Present: Commissioners Jason Hickman, Marguerite S. Lopez,
  Belen Zepeda; Vice Chair Paula Fraijo; Chair Dan Diaz

  Also present: Theresa Olivares, Assistant City Manager;
  Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager, Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public
  Works Services Manager; Pedro Rodriguez Jr., Public Works
  Maintenance Supervisor; and Armando Hegdahl, Management Analyst

SPONTANEOUS
COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  Lopez, to approve the Consent Calendar. The motion was unanimously
  approved.

ITEM NO. 1A  MINUTES
MINUTES
  The following minutes were approved as presented:

  1) Regular meeting held October 2, 2019.

NEW BUSINESS

ITEM NO. 2A  PROPOSED POLICY RELATED TO CITY SPONSORED EVENT
PROPOSED POLICY  VENDORS
RELATED TO CITY
SPONSORED EVENT
VENDORS

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda presented the staff report.
MANAGER ZEPEDA

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo spoke against requiring applicants to attend a
  mandatory vendor meetings, since it may deter individuals from
  participating and would needlessly complicate the process. She also
  suggested posting the policy and related documents online at the city’s
  website.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez concurred with Vice Chair Fraijo and suggested
LOPEZ  that participants be permitted to sign affidavits indicating that they have
  read the policy and agree to comply with program requirements.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  NOVEMBER 6, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 2

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Hickman suggested perhaps holding yearly meetings
HICKMAN  where participation is voluntary.

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares noted that the value of the meetings
MANAGER OLIVARES  would be that they allow participants to gain information on the program
  and ask any questions they may have. She further indicated that the
  program can be reviewed in a year to determine whether any changes
  would be necessary. Also, staff can develop a “Frequently Asked
  Questions” page on the city website that can help clarify the program
  requirements.

COMMISSIONER  Responding to a question by Commissioner Lopez, Recreation
LOPEZ  Manager Zepeda clarified the definitions of non-profits and vendors
  under the policy. Recreation Manager Zepeda also indicated that, in the
  past, the Teen Club has sold beverages for its fundraiser, but when
  non-profits began selling items at events, they were asked to refrain
  from selling beverages so that the Teen Club can conduct its fundraiser.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo questioned why certain elements of the policy were
  included, to which Recreation Manager Zepeda advised that the policy
  was drafted by incorporating elements from similar policies from other
  cities, and these were included in order to show the commission what
  other cities have implemented. Vice Chair Fraijo noted that there may
  be occasions where individual organizations should be able to
  exclusively sell certain items, and suggested that the section of the
  policy that prohibits this be stricken.

  Vice Chair Fraijo also asked about supplying power to vendor booths, to
  which Recreation Manager Zepeda indicated that the Public Works
  Department would usually supply power cords and lighting to vendor
  booths. Vice Chair Fraijo expressed concern over vendors potentially
  using their own damaged power cords, to which Assistant City Manager
  Olivares advised that staff could monitor booths to ensure its safety.
  Also, special event insurance is purchased for certain activities.

COMMISSIONER  Responding to a question by Commissioner Lopez, Assistant City
LOPEZ  Manager Olivares advised that health and safety permits restrict the
  preparation of food items to certain locations.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo suggested that sales be restricted to vendor booths,
  but that vendors be allowed to advertise their sales outside of the
  booths. She also asked which staff members would discuss the
  program requirements at the informational meetings, to which Assistant
  City Manager Olivares advised that staffing would vary depending on
  which department is holding the event.

  Vice Chair Fraijo also asked about vendor lotteries, to which Assistant
  City Manager Olivares advised that these would only be held to select
  which vendors may participate in events if there are not enough booths
  to accommodate all applicants. Vice Chair Fraijo then thanked staff for
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  NOVEMBER 6, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 3

  taking the initiative to prepare the policy, and suggested that the
  commission be permitted to modify the policy as it deems necessary.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Hickman suggested holding the optional information
HICKMAN  meeting for vendors every February.

MOTION  A motion was made by Vice Chair Fraijo, seconded by Commissioner
  Hickman, to modify the draft Vendor Policy by: 1) removing the
  stipulation that no vendor be the exclusive vendor of a specific item, 2)
  removing the requirement that information distribution be restricted to
  the designated booth area, 3) that the informational meetings for
  vendors be held every February, and that it be optional to attend, 4) that
  vendors be given the option to sign an affidavit attesting that they have
  read and understand the policy and agreed to abide by it, and 5) that
  the policy be reviewed next year to discuss whether any changes are
  necessary. The motion was unanimously approved.

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that an existing cell tower is
MANAGER OLIVARES  currently located within the Police Department parking lot, and that a
  request has been received to change the current tower with a new one.
  She then showed conceptual designs of what the new tower would look
  like compared to the existing one.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo asked about the reason behind the proposal, to which
  Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that there are many dead cell
  zones within the city. The goal is to install a new tower that would allow
  for better cell phone reception. The new pole also has the potential for
  increased revenue for the city.

  Responding to a question by Vice Chair Fraijo, Assistant City Manager
  Olivares advised that the new tower could potentially be made to
  resemble a palm tree. Vice Chair Fraijo expressed concern over
  potential negative health effects from the new pole, to which Assistant
  City Manager Olivares advised that she would need to research the
  concern.

COMMISSIONER LOPEZ  In answer to a question by Commissioner Lopez, Assistant City
  Manager Olivares advised that the city has a strong firewall to prevent
  hacking.

ITEM NO. 2C  IRWINDALE PARK PHASE IIB UPDATE
IRWINDALE PARK
PHASE IIB UPDATE

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares provided background information on
MANAGER OLIVARES  the project and made a PowerPoint presentation wherein she covered:
  1) an ADA path of travel throughout the park, 2) the removal of stairs
  on the west side of the Dan Diaz Recreation Building, 3) new
  landscaping on the west side of the Dan Diaz Recreation Building,
  4) enhanced lighting at the entrance of the Dan Diaz Recreation
  Building, 5) the design of the proposed bus shelter, 6) the design of
  the new picnic area near the horseshoe pit, 7) lighting at the picnic
  shelter, and 8) playground lighting.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo asked whether any grant funding is available for the
  project, to which Assistant City Manager Olivares indicated that she was
  not aware of any, though the Irwindale Community Foundation may
  provide some funding.

MANAGER RODRIGUEZ  Manager Rodriguez indicated that Measure A funding may also be
  available.

RECREATION
DEPARTMENT UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda reported the following:
MANAGER ZEPEDA
  1) Fifteen participants enjoyed the sold out Teen trip to Halloween
  Horror Nights.
  2) Twenty individuals participated in the Family trip to Oak Glen on
  October 19.
  3) Upcoming trips:
  A) Family Trip to LA Zoo – November 9
  B) Day Camp/Teen Trip to John’s Incredible Pizza – November 26.
  4) Participants of the Tiny Tots and Kidzone programs paraded through
  city departments and the Chamber of Commerce to trick or treat for
  Halloween.
  5) The Trunk or Treat event scheduled for October 31st was scheduled
  due to a lack of signups.
  6) Twenty-nine children registered to participate in the pumpkin
  decorating activity held on October 24.
  7) This year’s Halloween Spooktacular event is scheduled for October
  26.
  8) A Veterans’ Roll Call Ceremony has been scheduled for November
  11.
  9) The KidZone and all Tots classes will be closed the week of
  November 18.
  10) The Annual Christmas Spectacular and Mayor’s Christmas Tree
  Lighting Ceremony will be held on December 6.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  NOVEMBER 6, 2019
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 5

PUBLIC WORKS
DEPARTMENT UPDATE

PUBLIC WORKS MAINT.  Public Works Maintenance Supervisor Rodriguez reported the
SUP. RODRIGUEZ  following:

  1) Public Works crews assisted the Recreation Department in
  preparing for the recent Halloween Spooktacular. Public Works staff
  will also assist in setting up for the November 11 Veterans Day
  ceremony.
  2) Eleven residents attended the recent compost giveaway event at the
  Library.
  3) Public Works staff is working with the architect for the park
  improvement project to address lighting concerns at the park.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo spoke on the need for continued maintenance to
  ensure that the improvements that will be made at the park last as long
  as possible, to which Supervisor Rodriguez advised that he has staff
  attending classes on proper irrigation.

ASSISTANT CITY
MANAGER UPDATE

ASSISTANT CITY  Assistant City Manager Olivares advised that: 1) signups are being
MANAGER OLIVARES  accepted from staff to attend the December 5 Holiday Luncheon, and 2)
  the Senior Center will temporarily relocate to the Lark Ellen Welcome
  Center due to the upcoming Senior Center improvement project. She
  also spoke on the arrangements being made to continue existing senior
  programs and activities.

COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez asked about anti-bullying classes, to which
LOPEZ  Manager Zepeda advised they are held for the Day Camp trips, but not
  for the Kid Zone program. Commissioner Lopez requested that they
  also be held for school bus riders.

VICE CHAIR FRAIJO  Vice Chair Fraijo thanked staff for working well together to implement
  such wonderful programs that benefit the community.

CHAIR DIAZ  Chair Diaz also commended staff for the fantastic programs it prepares.

ADJOURNMENT  There being no further business to conduct, the meeting was adjourned
  at 7:07 p.m.
